statement: A random-initialized b5c48h3tfr exported by export_model_pytorch.py contains only block kinds transformer_attention_block / transformer_ffn_block and is accepted by cpp/neuralnet/desc.cpp (no 'unknown block kind'), running >0 visits/s in katago benchmark -boardsize 9.

With the mission selfplay_9x9.cfg (bSizes=9, bSizeRelProbs=1, allowRectangleProb=0) every SGF produced by katago selfplay carries SZ[9] and no other size appears (grep -L 'SZ\[9\]' over selfplay/*/sgfs returns nothing).

With dataBoardLen=9 in the selfplay cfg and -pos-len 9 in train.py, one shuffle + one training epoch complete on 9x9 data (data_processing_pytorch.py:91 shape assert passes, exit 0) and the npz row size is 2145 B uncompressed.

With numGameThreads=18, numSearchThreads=1, numNNServerThreadsPerModel=1 the live selfplay process has <= 24 OS threads (ps -o nlwp), and with numGameThreads=20 the gatekeeper has <= 24; train.py with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 stays <= 24.
One cycle of the mission synchronous loop (gatekeeper -> selfplay -> shuffle -> train -> export) completes on 1 GPU with tiny knobs and leaves a new models/<name>/model.bin.gz that katago loads.

Killing the loop job mid-train and mid-export and re-submitting resumes from checkpoint.ckpt with the same train_state row counter, loses no completed npz, and leaves no orphan *.exported dir that hides a checkpoint.

katago selfplay at production knobs (maxVisits 600, cheapSearchVisits 100, cheapSearchProb 0.75, numGameThreads 18) on one B200 sustains a measured and recorded games/hour and mean moves/game on 9x9; the 4-40x selfplay:train ratio is then re-derived from the measured train samples/s.

Recorded training rows per 9x9 game lie in [12, 35] (expected ~22 = ~0.27 rows/turn x ~80 turns, because cheapSearchTargetWeight=0 zeroes 75% of turns) and on-disk bytes per game are <= 10 KB at pos_len 9.

The whole mission fits in a 200 GB scratch budget: du -sb BASEDIR stays below 2.0e11 bytes across the run, with selfplay data < 20 GB per 10^6 games and checkpoints pruned to <= 4 short-term + <= 6 long-term.
Over the first 10 training epochs on 9x9 self-play data all logged loss terms in metrics_train.json are finite and the policy loss at epoch 10 is below its epoch-1 value.
The gatekeeper (200 games, win prop 0.5, 150 visits, 9x9) accepts at least 2 candidate nets after the first exported net, visible as >= 3 subdirs in models/ and gatekeepersgf logs.

In a katago match of 400 games on 9x9 (komi 7, maxVisits 150, both colors alternated) the latest accepted net beats the first exported net with win rate >= 0.60, whose 95% CI (SE 0.025 at n=400) excludes 0.5 (equivalently >= +70 Elo).

The v1.18.2 selfplay pipeline still implements these ideas from arXiv:1902.10565 under the cited config keys/code: playout cap randomization (cheapSearchProb/Visits/TargetWeight), forced root exploration (rootDesiredPerChildVisitsCoeff) with policy-target pruning (chosenMoveSubtract/Prune), auxiliary ownership/score/opponent-policy targets (metrics.py), score utility (staticScoreUtilityFactor/dynamicScoreUtilityFactor), lightweight gating; the residual-CNN trunk, the N_window formula and the 19x19 evaluation are superseded.

A second configuration (b7c96h3tfrs or b8c96h3tfrs, exportable attnrope+ffnsg) trains and exports in the same loop within <= 2 GPUs and 24 CPUs, and the loop's selfplay games/hour stays within 2x of the smoke config.

statement: export_model_pytorch.py refuses a checkpoint whose data-free attention logit bound exceeds -attn-logit-bound-limit 2.5e4 (model_pytorch.py:3010); the mission loop must either enable -attn-logit-penalty-cap in train.py (default off) or detect the refusal (export stage exit != 0) and record it in the error ledger rather than letting the loop die silently.

Decide and record USEGATING for the production loop: gating (200 games x 150 visits per candidate, ~0.53 acceptance at equal strength) costs a sizeable fraction of one GPU's selfplay budget; USEGATING=0 routes exports straight to models/ (export_model_for_selfplay.sh:115-120). Default design: USEGATING=1 for the smoke and first production run because eval_improvement (c13) counts acceptances; revisit at scale_up.
